measured_conclusion: The time-mean of the resolved run reproduces the steady solution: downforce differs by 8.6e-5 (0.0017 of the 0.005 bound) and Cd by 0.09%.

The steady ladder point is therefore NOT contaminated by unsteady content; the remaining V2->V3 downforce drift (0.0129-0.0147) is a refinement-family discretization effect, and per the pre-declared stop rules it stays above the registered bound with no further pre-declared factor left to isolate.
claims_supported: The steady fixed-domain reference at the reduced operating point is a valid time-mean of the laminar physics on the plain V2 mesh (numerical).
claims_not_supported: No grid-independent-downforce claim; the 0.005 bound remains unmet.
No high-Re or turbulent-shedding extrapolation (Re ~ 75 on the body length, laminar that the reduced case declares).
No claim about whether another mesh family could converge.
next: Per the WP3 stop rules: the fixed-domain ladder retains a measured downforce uncertainty band.
